title: What if the network was the sandbox? — Remy Guercio, Tailscale
talk_summary: Tailscale's Remy Guercio argues that identity-aware networking (WireGuard + Tailscale tags/ACLs) can serve as the sandbox boundary, and demos Aperture, an LLM gateway that holds the only provider API key while sandboxes connect with no key at all, tagged by identity. Because every model call must traverse the gateway, all tool calls, token usage, and costs are centrally visible and enforceable per identity/tag.

takeaways.technique: Keyless sandboxes behind a single-key LLM gateway
takeaways.what_they_do: Provider keys live only on the gateway node; agent sandboxes get a dummy key and a base URL, so there is no real credential inside the sandbox to exfiltrate or reuse against another endpoint.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's actually no key. It's just so like that runner connecting from the sandbox has no key to accidentally exfil

takeaways.technique: Per-identity and per-tag budgets across providers
takeaways.what_they_do: Gateway enforces quotas per user/agent tag and per model, with a shared pool that can be spent across any provider rather than fixed per-provider caps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's not like here's a thousand dollars for everybody. It's here's just a thousand dollars and you can decide to use it how you wish

takeaways.technique: Gateway-level capture of every tool call and request body
takeaways.what_they_do: Because all model traffic passes through the gateway, they log full request/response bodies and extract tool calls (bash, grep, MCP) centrally, independent of the harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have a sort of a guarantee uh that I've seen every tool call that this thing has ever like this thing has ever made

takeaways.technique: Cheap canary prompts to detect silent model drift
takeaways.what_they_do: They noticed a fixed trivial prompt's output shifted over weeks (robots to dogs to cats), using it as an informal drift signal, and saw the model fail a 10-word constraint.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if there's a sort of uh I don't know, model eval suite or something like that. I don't know. You can tell uh something's happening on the back end

takeaways.technique: Network-identity tags as the permission boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: Each sandbox/runner gets a tag (e.g. 'dogfood PR review bot') on the tailnet, and gateway rules key off that tag to decide model access and quotas.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that tag on the tailnet is what determines uh what it is able to do uh via or through Aperture

takeaways.technique: Webhooks on tool calls for external enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: Gateway fires webhooks per tool call with full metadata, giving a guaranteed hook point to react to or block actions like destructive bash commands.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we offer webhooks uh on top of this uh where for each of those tool calls ... you can actually send a request out to a third party
